LoRaWAN.definition: LoRaWAN is a low-power wide-area networking protocol designed to connect battery-operated devices to the internet through public, private or community networks.
LoRaWAN.deploymentFit: It is intended for IoT deployments that exchange relatively small amounts of data and need wide-area or difficult indoor coverage.
LoRaWAN.advantage: The standard is designed around range, device power use, network capacity and deployment cost.
LoRaWAN.limitation: Confirm that a suitable LoRaWAN network and the correct regional configuration are available for your project.

LTE CAT 1.definition: LTE Cat 1 is a 4G LTE device category first defined in 3GPP Release 8 and used by some IoT products.
LTE CAT 1.deploymentFit: It suits projects evaluating LTE cellular connectivity rather than the LPWA categories LTE-M or NB-IoT.
LTE CAT 1.advantage: It provides an LTE connectivity option for IoT devices.
LTE CAT 1.limitation: LTE Cat 1 is not interchangeable with LTE-M or NB-IoT. Confirm local operator service and model requirements before ordering.
LTE CAT 1.sourceLabel: GSMA — Mobile IoT in a 5G Future

NB-IoT.definition: NB-IoT is a 3GPP-standardised cellular low-power wide-area technology that operates in licensed spectrum.
NB-IoT.deploymentFit: It is intended for IoT devices with low-throughput requirements, including deployments seeking extended rural or indoor coverage.
NB-IoT.advantage: The technology is designed for low device complexity, power efficiency and large numbers of connected devices.
NB-IoT.limitation: Network availability and supported features vary by mobile operator and deployment, so they must be checked for the project location.

LTE-M & NB-IoT.definition: LTE-M and NB-IoT are complementary cellular low-power wide-area radio technologies specified by 3GPP.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.deploymentFit: They address IoT deployments needing licensed-spectrum wide-area connectivity, with the appropriate choice depending on device and network requirements.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.advantage: Products listing both technologies provide two cellular LPWA options to evaluate against local network support.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.limitation: Confirm supported modes, features and roaming arrangements with the mobile operator for your deployment.

LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.definition: LTE-M and NB-IoT are complementary cellular low-power wide-area radio technologies specified by 3GPP.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.deploymentFit: Consider these models when you need LTE-M or NB-IoT connectivity with the listed data bundle.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.advantage: These products provide both cellular LPWA options in the listed configuration.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.limitation: The label does not establish operator coverage, enabled features or fitness for a particular deployment.

NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.definition: NB-IoT is a 3GPP-standardised cellular low-power wide-area technology that operates in licensed spectrum.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.deploymentFit: Consider these models when you need NB-IoT connectivity with the listed data bundle.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.advantage: NB-IoT is designed for low-throughput, low-complexity IoT devices and extended coverage scenarios.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.limitation: The label does not establish operator coverage, enabled features or fitness for a particular deployment.

guides.title: How to Choose a LoRaWAN Gateway
guides.question: Which LoRaWAN gateway should I choose?
guides.answerTemplate: Choose from {count} LoRaWAN gateways. Start with the deployment setting and required backhaul: the catalogue includes indoor models such as LPS8N, LPS8v2, MS48-LR and LG308N, plus the outdoor DLOS8N. Then compare the exact gateway functions, interfaces, power details and ZAR price stated for the SKU.
considerations: Choose an indoor model when the deployment requires indoor gateway hardware; DLOS8N is the outdoor model in the exact product set.

Confirm the required IP backhaul. LPS8N, LPS8v2 and MS48-LR state Wi-Fi and Ethernet; LPS8N and LPS8v2 describe cellular as optional, while LG308N and DLOS8N state cellular connectivity in their product details.
Choose the function that matches the system: LPS8v2 includes local LoRaWAN and IoT server functions, while MS48-LR adds a Modbus gateway role and local server functions.
Check gateway management and deployment features where stated, including LPS8N web/SSH management, LPS8v2 remote management, and DLOS8N auto-provisioning and remote monitoring.
Confirm the regional LoRaWAN frequency configuration, supplied power requirement, package details and exact SKU before ordering.
guides.differenceSummary: The catalogue contains indoor and outdoor gateway options. LPS8N bridges LoRaWAN to IP through Wi-Fi or Ethernet, with an optional cellular version. LPS8v2 adds local LoRaWAN and IoT server functions and also describes optional 4G. MS48-LR combines gateway, local server and Modbus functions with optional 4G. LG308N lists Wi-Fi, Ethernet and cellular backhaul, while DLOS8N is the outdoor model and lists cellular failover as optional alongside outdoor deployment features. Other rows should be checked by their exact supplied specification.
decisionPath: Decide whether the gateway must be indoor or outdoor, then shortlist the models whose product details match that setting.
Select the required backhaul: Wi-Fi or Ethernet, with optional cellular where the exact model supports it and the deployment requires it.
Choose any local server, Modbus, management or outdoor feature only when the exact SKU states it.
Confirm regional frequency, power, package information and price for the exact SKU before ordering.

guides.title: Compare DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 Distance Sensors
guides.question: How do DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 distance sensors differ?
guides.answerTemplate: DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 are ultrasonic distance-sensing product lines. DDS20 is for non-contact liquid-level measurement through a container over 20mm to 2000mm. DDS45 and DDS75 measure distance to a flat object, with catalogue ranges of 30mm to 4500mm and 280mm to 7500mm respectively.
considerations: Choose DDS20 when the measurement is liquid level through a container without contacting the liquid.
Choose between DDS45 and DDS75 by the flat-object range and measurement angle required: 30mm to 4500mm at 60° for DDS45, or 280mm to 7500mm at 40° for DDS75.
Compare the exact SKU connectivity shown in the catalogue, including LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, LTE-M & NB-IoT, and LTE CAT 1 variants.
For LB and LS variants, compare the exact power entry: 8500mAh for LB or solar panel plus 3000mAh Li-ion battery for LS.
Confirm the target or container arrangement, required range, regional connectivity variant, and exact SKU before ordering.
guides.differenceSummary: DDS20 measures liquid level through a container without contacting the liquid. DDS45 and DDS75 measure distance to a flat object. DDS45 covers the shorter 30mm to 4500mm catalogue range with a 60° angle, while DDS75 covers 280mm to 7500mm with a 40° angle. Connectivity and power options vary by exact SKU.
decisionPath: Identify whether the project measures liquid level through a container or distance to a flat object.
For flat-object measurement, compare the required range and angle against DDS45 and DDS75 catalogue values.
Select the exact connectivity and power variant, then confirm the full catalogue row before ordering.
